invented.where: First reply ("The idea") and third reply (section 1, and the handwriting font reserved for "her two direct quotes")

invented.claim: A causal chain she never claims: "a near-miss that turned into a redesign that turned into a measurable result (71%→94% scanning compliance)" — conflates the handover-sheet redesign with the scanning figure, which came from the workarounds study.

final.question: A clinical shift, told in audit-cycle order (Plan → Do → Study → Act), proving the same thing twice: once as a story, once as a method
final.form: The nursing audit cycle — Plan, Do, Study, Act — names sections 3 to 5, and the ISBAR handover form (Identify, Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) gives section 4 its five beats
final.object: An ECG trace drawn as a vertical "spine" down the page: one spike at the near-miss, three branch ticks for the three workarounds, a steady brightening at the result, terminating at "Now"

swap.reason: The scroll is built on her own observational study — forty hours, the three named workarounds, the scanners moved to the medication room door, the ISBAR sheet she led — not a structure that would survive being dropped onto another informatics nurse's site.

backdrop.reason: The hero wristband is admitted to be ambient ("It doesn't react to scroll... it's just present"), the spine carries mood the copy already carries, and the handover sheet would read the same as a flat image with the old/new toggle.

depth.reason: Why → Plan → Do → Study/Act → Now → Close is causally ordered and cannot be shuffled without breaking the audit cycle it names.

clipart.reason: The one object that persists and changes across the scroll is a glowing heartbeat/ECG line, the stock emblem of healthcare, while the more specific barcode wristband leaves the screen after section 1.

honesty.reason: The final plan uses CNM1 and Nursing Informatics Link Nurse, credits 71→94 to the ward with her part named, credits the sheet to a group of five, drops the whiteboard photo, and strips the near-miss of identifying detail.

thirty_seconds.reason: Section 1 deliberately has "no nav yet" and only a scroll arrow, the jump-menu appears only after the opener, and CV, email and LinkedIn exist only in section 7, so a non-scroller gets name and role but no proof and no way to make contact.

plain_reader.reason: The opening is her name, her real title, the hospital, a plainly worded line about safe versus slow, and a one-line hiring status — readable by a health-tech recruiter and credible to a nurse.

judgement.summary: This is a single-column, long-form scroll that retells Aoife Brennan's barcode-scanning study in the order of the nursing audit cycle (Plan, Do, Study, Act), with the ISBAR letters structuring the handover-sheet section, an ECG line as the page's spine, and a correct, well-corrected account of her title and of whose result the 71→94 figure was. Its greatest weakness is that the 3D is largely atmosphere rather than argument — the persistent object is the most clichéd healthcare motif there is, the hero wristband is explicitly inert, and the opening section withholds proof and contact from anyone who does not scroll.
